real_conflicts: The Editorial Director and Information Architect propose moving the 'Read the Issue' button to the top-right header area. This is a production failure; placing a primary conversion action in the header of a single-page editorial layout creates a 'floating' UI element that lacks visual anchoring and disrupts the reading flow. The button must remain at the bottom to serve as a conclusion to the content hierarchy.

The Art Director's proposal to use 'overlapping translucent gradients' and 'organic curves' for the background risks introducing rendering inconsistencies and visual noise that will degrade the legibility of the body text. The current dot-grid is a safe, scalable pattern that ensures the text remains crisp against the background.
accepted: The Editorial Director's proposal to move the Feature Essay to the top-left quadrant is accepted. The current bottom-left placement creates a disjointed reading path that forces the eye to jump around the page. A top-left anchor is standard for editorial grids and ensures the feature story is the first thing the reader encounters.

The Information Architect's proposal to restructure the secondary articles into a 2x2 grid is accepted. The current single-column list with horizontal dividers creates a 'spreadsheet' aesthetic that contradicts the 'expressive composition' mandate. A grid layout allows for better use of whitespace and visual balance.
concession: I concede that the current 'solid dark' button is visually heavy and the horizontal dividers in the secondary column are too mechanical. I agree to replace the solid button with a high-contrast outlined (stroke) button and remove the horizontal rules in favor of vertical spacing.
compromise: We will implement the 2x2 grid for secondary articles as requested by the IA, but we will strictly enforce a uniform typographic system across all four items to maintain the 'coherent editorial system' mandate. We will not use the Art Director's 'distinct typographic treatments' (e.g., different fonts for poetry) as this creates a fragmented design language. Instead, we will use category labels (e.g., 'Fiction', 'Poetry') in a consistent accent color to differentiate content.
nonnegotiable: The 'Read the Issue' button must remain in the bottom-left area, adjacent to the feature story text, to maintain the logical conclusion of the reading path.
